description:
PayStream are one of the leading providers of limited company, umbrella company & back office services to both contractors and recruitment agencies. From the moment you sign up, you can expect nothing less than outstanding service, sound advice and straight-talking answers to your questions from a company that's run by qualified accountants. 


Here are ten reasons why choosing PayStream makes Perfect Sense to contractors…


1. Brilliant customer service matters to us. A lot. We're proud to be fully accredited by Customer Service Excellence - the most reputable body in the field - as well as other key industry bodies like APSCo and FCSA. We've also been voted Best Umbrella Company (three times overall), Best Contractor Accountancy (four times overall), Best Verification & Screening Provider (for our Candidate Screening service) and Best Contractor Innovation (for our IR35 Comply review service) in The Contracting Awards over the years. 


2. We're run by qualified accountants, meaning we're are always on top of industry legislation changes, ensuring that you are in the right service for your circumstance.


3. We've created our own suite of slick, efficient and user-friendly online tools that have been designed to make your life easier, and are constantly being updated by our in-house development team.


4. Our hand-picked team of experts have over 30 years' experience at the height of the legal and accountancy professions. We work relentlessly to stay at the top of our game, keeping up to date with legislation and working with our advisors and HMRC to ensure you get the best and most compliant solutions in the market.


5. Our contractors benefit from special access to our employee reward scheme, with over 2000 offers that aren't publicly available.


6. Unlike many umbrella companies, we're here to stay - with a highly motivated workforce of over 250 and counting.


7. We offer every type of accounting and payroll service you'll ever need as a contractor. So you can keep your pay hassle-free however your career develops.


8. Whatever your industry - IT, education, construction, you name it - we've got the experience and know how to guide you.

I suspect they are playing catch-up with outstanding expenses from their customer base but it’s quite frustrating to be paid expenses, and not receive the tax relief in the same month. It’s all getting a bit messy. PLEASE CATCHUP PAYSTREAM. UPDATE 26 July - that’s another month processed without any tax relief. Now over 2 months behind. records.title: For anyone setting up a new company they are great
records.text: For anyone setting up a new company paystream are a great option. They do everything for you including all the relevant documentation, registrations etc. to make it all easy. They have a great team of people who are easily accessible on the phone and offer great advice. The online platform is excellent which shows your P&L in an easy to understand format and all your expenses can be managed through this too. This links to your business bank account so everything is seamless. At the end of the year they complete the company accounts and help and offer advice to be tax efficient within the confines of the law. records.title: Issues Payslips
records.text: To be honest, my experience with Paystream was super stressful for most of the payments. Some payslips came out correct. I was penalized for having my direct debit delayed and I only received APOLOGIES. Other than that, Customer Service is proactive. records.title: Bad experience
records.text: It seems most people are happy with Paystream but i have had a horrible experience . My payment was missed on a Friday due to late approval of my timesheet . It then resulted in me getting paid twice the following week. When i got paid that following week i noted  my  payment was short of 300 pounds. When I wrote to them they simply replied that i should contact HMRC to change my tax code which does not make sense .The issue is purely administrative . Someone should have understood that i was getting paid twice because a payment had been missed the previous week and do the adjustment . Paystream was very unhelpful. And will not be able to recommend them .It may be that the team are with are not as professional as others

records.title: There were repeated calls for already…

records.title: Payroll normally goes OK but there are issues
records.text: Payroll normally goes OK, you get paid usually 2-3 weeks after the client has paid, minus the 50 odd percent tax of course.Setting up a private pension contribution takes forever, in my case about 6 months so I lost a significant contribution to my pension  and associated tax relief.They also have constraints around pensions in that you can't make a fixed contribution each month, neither can you make a lump sum contribution. Lots of red tape and explanations are needed to do anything in this area despite it being YOUR money. Expenses are a problem and not easy to get paid out.Think of Paystream as an agent for HMRC simply there to collect tax but offer you little support. They are your 'employer' only when it suits them - auto enrolling you in their pension scheme and trying to withold holiday pay etc.The madness of IR35 means you pay somebody to 'employ' you and treat you like a young child. Two stars for the payroll, very little else to recommend here other than the staff are friendly, if ineffective. I will be leaving (or should that be 'resigning') very soon...*****EDIT JAN 24******I have been in touch with a dedicated team leader who is helping to resolve issues discussed above and looking at ways to improve the immediate situation and evolve other aspects. Jack has been a great help, and clearly understands the situation. This gives me confidence that they are working to tighten up on the grumble areas, albeit within the inevitable limitations of the regulators. Bumped up to 3 stars, I feel a 4 is incoming...

records.title: Good if you like gambling sites.
records.text: First few levels were fine and earned a few pounds, but as you progress most of the levels involve signing up for gambling sites (especially level 8). As someone who does not gamble, I was unable to progress as I do not have pets so no point signing up for flea treatment. Such a shame as I thought there would be more surveys and such.Also not sure if it's related but since signing up through this site, I have had so many spam phone calls.

records.title: I like the fact I actually got paid but…
records.text: I like the fact I actually got paid but honestly I’d say my experience was more bad than good. I think a lot of the tasks could be better, a few of them I did never actually come up as completed even though I did them, a fair few of the tasks are linked to gambling which I think is just enticing people to sign up to various different sites and gamble which I don’t really agree with. Some of the tasks actually ask you to sign up and pay for something for say £20 but then only pay you £7.50 for completing it which just makes no sense then your actually losing money. Lastly the tasks don’t get changed often enough to be able to make anywhere near the average that the cash back app states. It’s worth doing in your spare time but it definitely could be better.

records.title: Extremely baffling and time-consuming, but worth it if you're very bored and want £30 for a week's work
records.text: Hmm, there's a lot to consider when it comes to Cashback and I haven't got time to mention it all. But I'd say:PROS: 1) An ok project if you need some money.2) Customer service are fairly good. They do reply to you at least, and helped me out on a few occasions.CONS: 1) You do actually have to work for the money (which they don't tell you), because you have to keep track of all the different things you need to sign up for, and make sure you cancel at the right time. I fell foul of this a couple of times, so paid for subscriptions that I didn't need.2) Most of the tasks (especially the gambling ones) require you to pay some money. You will make a profit in the end if you do it properly, but you'll need the money in the first place.3) There's a minefield of smallprint; read it thoroughly. I didn't get paid for a few tasks because I didn't follow the instructions properly.4) I paid out about £80 and earned £154. So that's £74 profit. It's impossible to calculate accurately, but the time I spent faffing around with it all - plus the time it took up in my brain's life when I wasn't actively playing the games etc - amounted to about 2 weeks' work in total. And that's being generous. So I earned roughly £37 for a week's work. That's what you're dealing with here.

records.title: Mediocre
records.text: Mediocre. I have been using cashback for 2 months now. Listen, it works yes. I got paid around 50-60 somewhat the first time I used it and I was happy. Used the money to buy gifts for the family. However, you cannot use it again. For example, the subscription ones like ON THAT ASS and Amazon Prime. You cannot do them again because your card is linked already. I also had a very bad problem with ON THAT ASS. Tell me why to cancel the subscription I have to do it a month before? It does not make sense. If u don't do it a month before it forces u to pay. I would like cashback to remove on that ass on their feed because it's just scamming people. Another problem is the high amounts of pay to earn. I came into cashback to make money. Imagine going to a job and they ask you to pay a sum of money to make like 5 pounds more than the sum. That's not how it works. In the beginning of cashback i asked for surveys. I have not seen 1 task that includes surveys. It's filled with pay 10 pounds to make 15 and stuff it's ludicrous.

records.title: Very disappointed!!!

records.title: Massive waste of time

Because the delay was so long and I'm talking up to a week in the beginning and so that I didn't lose track of which ones I had completed I started sending them proof as I went along. records.title: If you want to go the gambling route-…
records.text: If you want to go the gambling route- please bear in mind that a lot of the sites don't accept Mastercard. You will go through the signing up process and likely be plagued with unwanted emails thereafter until you can be bothered to unsubscribe/ delete your account, yet be rejected because you can't deposit. You also have to be a new customer for many of these offers.I appreciate a lot of this is likely explained in the terms and conditions and I'm sure some people have success with the site. It's money for nothing to an extent- however- you can easily end up wasting lots of time and money that you won't get back unless you are willing to put in a lot more time and hassle to complete every task.

records.title: Please read before you think about going ahead - honest review
records.text: Some things you need to be aware of before you do this Iva. - They ask for rough ideas of what you pay on things, no it’s not - be exact because in some cases they will check and ask more money off you.- if you get a pay-rise/promotion (I worked so hard for many years for this) you have to give that extra money to them.- they will make you feel guilty over and over again (they say the only reason I get to keep my car is because of them) so have a thick skin. We had our little boys 3rd birthday I said to him what about if we want to spend a little more on that he goes money was set out for that (no word of a lie I think I just said a high number the guy goes that’s a bit much for that I said have you been to Lego land recently?! So they made me put the number down so the guy goes you have the figure in your paper work I was like what?! We have to stick to a certain amount a month for ‘child’s fun’ it’s crazy.- they say these things are for people who can actually afford to pay their bills just left with minimum income at the end but as soon as you start to have a little more they will take take take still resolving in not being able to save any money.- they will say anything to get you to agree it but don’t rush you decision I deffo felt pressured into this I was literally crying down the phone to this guy I was so upset about everything and he goes ‘well I don’t want to do all this work if you’re going to say no’ - the first amount they say you will have to pay is not the amount it goes up and up and up.- think about all your options before going with this company of an Iva in all, it is still the most stressful thing in my life even after getting into an Iva that is meant to help me. If you can afford to pay all the bills but only left with a little just ride it out for as long as you can and watch the payments come down. This will only help you if you are looking to stay in the same job for the next 6 years and you are at the end of your limits with not having any money left after paying your bill, if you are the type of person who pays the exact amount of the exact same things every month this will help you. If you have a non robotic life and can’t tell from month to month what’s going to happen (my car broke down and cost 400 to fix, funny how they didn’t ask to factor that in) then think again, please only do this if you really really trusty need it.

After speaking to Daniel (shout out to you, you've been amazing) and Sarah (you've been amazing), Sarah put me through to the DRO specialist that brushed me off by saying just go on our website. Terrible, I feel like that lady from DRO (didn't introduce herself) didn't want to do her job, just wanted to get quickly of the phone. No you don't have lady called Sarah on NDH she was from the company you collaborate with

records.title: Nuisance call company!
records.text: Started nuisance calling my mobile the day before the arranged appointment. They didn't letting it ring for more than 1-2 seconds before sending me a text to say that they try and called and to reply yes or no. Just another one bell nuisance call company!In reply. Your staff made the choice to end the call after one ring (on my end), this I'm sure because it's quicker to end the call and send a text allowing staff to get through more enquiries.I made a phone appointment, so why would I need to be called before that? Then I have to take time to call the number back! You didn't even honor the agreed upon appointment as no call was received at the time it was arranged.When a company one bells you then hangs up it is a nuisance call, to suggest that the call just ended is dishonest and a lie to all those which read your reply.

records.title: Do not trust these people!
records.text: Do not trust these people. They come across very nice and helpful but they will rip you off, bombard you with calls if you change your mind to the point of being harrasing, even aggressive when I told Daniel (pre contract) I had changed my mind. After apparently disposing of my details I still get calls a year on! These people also trade under other company names. Please think... for a national company why does Daniel always appear to answer the phone then Sadaf is always next. Also look out for Sarah who supposedly calls you back from another sister company but is really sitting with them. Please think twice you will get in more debt when they keep assessing your income each month and put  your disposal income up which means more free money to pay them and not a lot going to debt consoladation. Call each of your creditors independantly, explain your situation and that you are calling all creditors. You will be surprised how understanding they are. You can set your own affordable payment amount and you will be comforted to know all your money would be going to pay off debts and not to these con artists. Yes it may take some time but it will definitely be worth it.

records.title: Don't use this firm
records.text: Don't use this firm, service was not good at all. Phoned on behalf of my mum, and spoke to Daniel. He seemed very condescending and rude, and when he called her back an hr before he was meant to, she felt pressured to do things then and there. Name is national debt help but I can't see it being recommended by any authorities as a national helpline. My mother has now been in touch with a proper helpline, who have been helpful and kind.

records.title: Avoid Using
records.text: If you think its bad getting phone calls from Creiditors, thats nothing compaird to what this company do, even once you have paid. In the 8 months I was with them, 5 times I have been chased for payment after it was sent. 3 of them times, their bank put it into a holding account, and returned it after about 2 weeks. Twice I was getting calls asking for payments made 2-3 days before, AS THEY HAD NOT UPDATED THEIR RECORDS. At 8am they will call 1 of your numbers, and 5 min later, the other number they have for you. Your credit file is not better off for using them, as they take their fees in full before anything gets paid off, so in my case over £1000 paid and no payments reported to my credit file.

records.title: Disappointing service, I would not recommend them.
records.text: *** JSA completed my SATR on 23/02/2022.  I was charged £5.84 interest for late payment on account by the HMRC.  I am glad that I wasn't fined more, but this should never have happened.  I gave JSA all the information they needed on 26/11/2021 to complete my SATR. They caused me unnecessary stress.  Giving them 2 stars instead of 1, as Donna and Dawn did return my calls so I wasn't ignored.** Update. Spoke to Donna who is the manager of my personal accountant Dawn.  I was told they would update me today (22/02/2022), but nothing. I still don't know if they will finish my SATR before 28/02/2022.  That means I may be charged £100 by the HMRC for late filing. Absolutely disgraceful service.  *Update.  My self-assessment tax return for 2021 is still not ready.  I chased for an update today (18/02/2022) and they told me it would be ready by 24/02/2022.  I wonder if JSA has missed the SATR deadline of 31/01/2022 for anyone else or is it just me? Very disappointing service...I have employed JSA Services to complete my self-assessment tax return for 2020-2021.  Having my own full time job, 2 kids and moving home I thought it would be easier to have my accountant submit it.  Not wanting to miss the SATR deadline, I sent all my information to JSA on 26/11/2021.  I sent a few email chasers in January to find out when my SATR would be ready.  I was initially told it would be done before 31/01/2022.  I wasn't too worried so I waited.  A few days before the deadline I asked again about my SATR and I was still told it would be ready by 31/01/2022.  I called up on Friday (28/01/2022) about it and this time I was told that JSA would work through the weekend to have it completed.  I thought this was strange as I sent my information back in 26/11/2021.  Fair enough I thought, my accountant told me about delays due to Covid.  Not surprisingly, on 31/01/2022 I received an email telling me that my SATR would not be completed in time and my accountant expressed that the HMRC deadline was extended to 28/02/2022.  I finally received my SATR on 03/02/2022.  Due to my own work commitments (also affected by Covid), 2 kids and house move I only finished reviewing my SATR today (11/02/2022) and I am disappointed that they missed so many items.  Over 2 months and JSA did not once request any additional information from me and I had to spend hours of my own time reviewing it.  Hopefully JSA will get my SATR finished soon so I won’t be charged too much interest on the late payment. And this isn't my first disappointing encounter with JSA.  I recently closed my Ltd company and JSA were delayed in completing my cessation accounts, but that's another story which they did resolve quickly when I complained.  And don't mention when JSA took over CleverAccounts and messed up my accounting data.

records.text: Very sadly, Salad do not lend to those who get paid weekly…period. I meet and significantly exceed their monthly income requirement of £1300 per month, but that has been completely and disappointingly disregarded. I have looked at their explanation for this; they are unable to align their collection date with a monthly pay date? However, in my case they have four potential dates to choose from, so I’m not entirely convinced by this. Also generally speaking, there is usually a provision made by lenders to allow their customers to decide the most convenient date for their monthly repayments, as they may have other financial obligations to budget for and therefore may wish to stagger payments rather than have one big hit on payday? Salad should in my view not assume they can make a collection on payday (unless they are marketing their product as a ‘payday loan’, which I don’t believe they do?). It seems very unfortunate that the company implement a very clearly defined double standard with regard to people in my position, when it would seem they generally provide a  decent service to many who apply. Very disappointing!!

records.title: Don't leave your session for too long
records.text: I'm sure this service is great if you are exchanging a few bank notes. In my case I was getting rid of old coins from a lifetime of travelling. TLDR: mediocre review because I had to enter all my data twiceThe positives are that I could get something out of small change that's not catered for by any other service I am aware of, including pre-Euro currency. Minor inconveniences were :• Postage costs wipe out any gains from posting coins, unless you have a LOT of coins or quite a few high value coins. Luckily I was driving past and I delivered it myself. • I had to enter my data twice (see below). In between the value of GBP tanked because of high profile actions of our inept government. GBP fell by several percent against a range of currencies. Yet the quoted price remained the same. I realise there is manual intervention required for this sort of exchange and this has a cost. Businesses like this need to make a profit in order to keep providing this useful service. The website strongly suggests that they respond to currency movements and that your price is "locked in" for a limited time while they wait for your cash to arrive. If this isn't the case for, for example, pre-euro currency, they should be upfront about this. • Major inconvenience: Without this I would have rated this business 4 or 5 stars. I started selecting coins and inputting numbers into the website. I saw there was a session based "wallet" a bit like a shopping basket on any e-commerce website. When finished, I left my tab open, refreshed it the next day, the content was still there. I thought I'd leave it till the weekend to look for more old coins. When I found them and came back to complete the process the wallet was empty. I didn't clear cookies or anything. As this was a one-off, I didn't feel the need to create an account. The transient nature of the wallet contents should be advertised prominently. I often find my basket with things in it after months on other sites I don't have an account with, perhaps I was a little too optimistic. I had to enter data on 100+ coins a second time, just to get a few pounds, which was very frustrating

records.text: I had some old French francs which I found at my Dads house after he sadly passed away.  I was not overly expecting any return on them but banks seemed reluctant to take them.  When I found Leftover Currency it seemed a perfect solution.  I filled out the form, sent the currency & received a cheque in the post (not much but that wasn't the point). Downside was when I went to pay the money into my bank THE ACCOUNT HAD BEEN CLOSED & so in the end I received nothing which left a bad taste in my mouth about the trustworthy operations of this company.  I would not use them again as a result & would suggest if you do need any money as a result of currency exchange DO NOT USE THEM.

records.title: Two points
records.text: Two points: firstly, when I sent emails I frequently received a notification that the email had not been received. However when I queried I was told that everything was OK. Confusing and worrying. Secondly, only upon acceptance of the accounts and go ahead to submit them to Companies House did I find out that in order to submit them to HMRC I needed to wait to receive a code in order to do so. When I contacted Debitam to begin with I asked specifically to be talked through the process, since this is the first time I have done this for a company, and company accounts were due to be filed very quickly. Thankfully I requested an extension on the filing which was accepted, so no harm done. But not good to find this out at the last minute, when I had asked for step by step procedure. I'm still not clear whether this code for HMRC is one-off or will be required every time I submit company accounts.

records.title: Accounting work is good, pre-sales aggressive tactics less appealing
records.text: The actual accountancy side of things was quite straight forward and improved over the last couple of years with better online tools to work through the process.My main issue is that there is a very hard sell to get you to sign up - emails saying that you are close to the HMRC deadline and if you go over it you'll probably get fined, hurry hurry hurry. To the point where you get emails every other days, constant emails trying to get you to pay for the service. But one person on the phone let slip that were just trying to hit monthly targets on sign ups, so its obvious the angle.Then what makes it worse is the when you do finally commit and pay the invoice they are very calm about getting the accounts finalised - that's not to say they are moving forward with it all but when I delays getting back to them with information or tweaking items in Xero, they suddenly didn't seemed so worried that we were about to go over the HMRC deadline. Now its wasn't critical!! I wish they were as worried about my accounts actually get filled as they were about getting paid.Having said all this, I know this what they are like so I will probably use them again but I don't like the ethos and I'd use another company if they offered a similar service.

records.title: Price was good however I felt the…

I was asked to supply them with login details to send the CT600 form and once I found out and advised it was something they do it was done instantly. There was a VAT discrepancy and I had no idea how to handle it so I had to speak to the previous accountant who advised the solution.

records.title: Playing on your ignorance
records.text: If you've never done a Confirmation Statement Filings before and your company is dormant, it can take less than 5 minutes to do this online at Companies House, and costs £13. They even have a video to show you how.This company's "core offerings" include a £49+vat to do the Confirmation Statement Filing for you. Maybe they're useful for people with active companies, but you're simply being taken advantage of if you use this service for never used dormant accounts.

In my latest tax return the inclusion of gift aid payments resulted in an underpayment of tax. I was a little disappointed that this was not questioned when the return was being prepared, as these were in joint names and could be applied to my wife’s tax account. Perhaps I am only paying for a basic service, however, for £800 a year I feel I should receive more advice.

description:
Unbiased connects you to the UK’s biggest selection of financial advisers, mortgage brokers, solicitors and accountants
We have a network of 27,000 professional expert advisers
Over 10 million customers have found advice with Unbiased
Our unique matching tool finds you the best match based on your needs

records.title: First time user of Unbiased.com
records.text: I have not used the site before and found it difficult to negotiate initially. It took some time to find what I was looking for, an IFA. The IFA was quick to respond but didn’t provide me sufficient detail to make an informed decision on the way forward. I intend to go back in and take more time to look through the site.

records.title: Abit hit and miss…
records.text: I don't find it particularly easy to use as I am presented with a list of IFAs, with very little available to make a choice of which one to use. records.title: New appointment
records.text: My Call from Standard life on Monday advised me that the Hub would call me on Wednesday.  Didn't get a Call until Thursday  I contacted Unbiased on Thursday got a message that a financial adviser had been found and they would contact me soon.  Didn't get any contact until I had a text on Saturday to ask if they could ring me on Monday.  Got an appointment Thursday evening, a week after my request to Unbiased.

records.title: Need more options about who/who not to contact and time limits for response
records.text: Selected an advisor who unfortunately didn't get back to me within whatever time limit set by unbiased. The enquiry was then passed to somebody I didn't want to contact - platform needs to check with you first whether you want to do this. Used another platform to find an advisor in the end.

records.title: Didn't suit me
records.text: I would have preferred to read some bio-data so I could choose who to approach rather than submit my details for all and sundry. The only call I got was an answerphone message with a lot of background noise so I was unable to hear the number.

records.title: So far I have not been able to get in…
records.text: So far I have not been able to get in touch with advisor.Although quick to get someone at first it has not worked out to this point.  I will try again after the holidays.  Should I start over or carry on from where it left off?BestRory

records.title: Efficient service
records.text: Was a very fast response and the advisor has been very helpful. My particular circumstances didn't clearly meet the tick box choices on your site so had to guess which one to put, might be good to have a space for someone to write any extra info/ requests  they might have

records.title: Need to back up words with deeds
records.text: I think that as with a lot of organisations, the emphasis is on getting customers, which clearly is great. However as again with a lot of organisations, there is a lack of follow up and continuity. So the web site sets you up well, but the back story doesn't support this approach anywhere near as well as it should.

records.title: To be fair
records.text: To be fair, I had to ask the Financial Advisor to ring back due to work commitments, which he did.It took me a while to find my pension forecast but once I had it, all I learned was that LGPS was one of the better pensions to be with.  The advisor offered nothing with regards to advice on whether I should be paying more or not and how much I was likely to get when I retire? Or if I could retire early etcDisappointing to be honest.

records.title: Not quite independent advice
records.text: I found it easy to use, but it didn't meet my needs. I was looking for an Independent Financial Advisor, with an emphasis on independence. The person I spoke to was professionally competent and represented a very credible company, but I can't help but feel a little concerned when the Financial Advisor that reaches out to me represents a specific financial institution. This was my second attempt to find an IFA (I used another site previously) And on that occasion, they represented SJP the advice on the whole again was good but involved moving all my money over to them. While the advice may not be bad, it feels more like I am being sold to than advised.

records.title: Quick and easy but comms could be better
records.text: It was quick and easy. Within 24 hours a potential supplier had been identified. However, they did not check back on the app after first contacting me so my subsequent attempts at comms with them went unanswered. This aspect could be improved. Thanks

records.title: I was looking for a recommended accountant …
records.text: I was looking for a recommended accountant to assist with my self assessment tax returns but they were unable to find one anywhere in Brighton which was disappointing

records.title: Unbiased are a business, not part of a Government scheme
records.text: The Financial Advisors I met through Unbiased were excellent. EST based off the Llantrisant Road, Cardiff could not have been better informed and My advisor, Chris Woods, took time to understand my situation, and approach to my pension etc - and came up with a solutions I did not know existed and which fits my needs perfectly.But I had not realised that Unbiased was not a Government Scheme and are offering this introduction service simply as a money making business. It's a shame.

records.title: Very limited scope of results
records.text: I was looking for a local accountant, for general accountancy, nothing specialised.   I thought unbiased would help me find some local ones and save me some time.  All I got matched up with was 2 companies 450 miles away and although separate companies had the same accountant working for them.  So all in I feel disappointed that they either do not have a large list of people they deal with, or have a select few that pay them for.  Not a really helpful situation my me and my needs

records.title: Ho hum
records.text: Ho hum, another pointless website that any self respecting supplier would avoid, like Rated people and Checkatrade. The only people I found  on those two sites were either desperate or incompetent. On this site there were precisely zero. I'm sure for some people it works occasionally so good for you but this particular boat has not only not sailed, it sank at the dockside.

records.title: Unbiased/ not unbiased
records.text: Unbiased are not unbiased. For example they even go as far as misrepresenting trust pilot scores by stating 3 stars are bad and 4 are average ....wrong.After asking for a local IFA recommendation they consistently recommended a large company some 60 miles away....I wonder why. Make your own mind up and use this 'tool ' carefully.They will give you lists of IFAs but beware they may just direct you to the large companies.

records.title: Unsatisfactory
records.text: Web portal was simple enough. Someone was in touch within a couple of days.Unfortunately he suggested a place and time that was way too soon for me, given that I've reached out to more than one source for advice. When I let him know this he told me I should go with my other options and he would delete my details. No flexibility or alternative offered.I am now pursuing an alternative solution.

records.title: Local is Hard. It was actually very hard to find a…
records.text: It was actually very hard to find a service that was truly local. Lots of big nationwide firms have loaded the Unbiased database with locations and cities where they don't actually have a presence. Finding a service that was really based in offices on the Isle of Wight was hard as so many of the adverts were misleading. If you don't mind a supplier the other end of the UK from you its fine.

records.title: Wanted a LOCAL accountant, not one 120 miles away
records.text: I was looking for a local account who could assist with self assessment to include management of pension tax / possible emergency tax code.  I waited several days to be informed that the closest accountant was 120 miles away .. I don't live on the moon, I live in a large town in Kent .. I'd expected a company within a 15 mile radius so I can visit them / deal with my tax face-2-face.  Very disappointed with Unbiased .. there are alternative sites that help identify independent advice / accounts, will use these from now on.

records.title: Not unbiased
records.text: I was pleased to be quickly matched with an advisor, who made an appointment with me the same day. However, the advice was really just an attempt to get me to sign up for a comprehensive wealth management solution that was way beyond my requirements.I came looking for 'unbiased' advice, so was disappointed to be matched with a clearly very biased advisor.I understand there's a way to request a new advisor, but I have no reason to think the next one won't have the same agenda.Decided to go back to searching manually for an truly unbiased advisor.

records.title: Bit of a Hit-and-Miss Process
records.text: Unbiased matched me up with an adviser from a local business, Flying Colours. Despite the information I submitted in advance -- including that my pension pot amounted to just over £50K and that I was looking for a particular type of annuity -- I was told (in the nicest of terms) that they wouldn't consider anyone with pension savings under £75K. As it wouldn't be financially viable for them.So, a mis-match and something of a waste of time. There is clearly an element of hit-and-miss serendipity to the process.That said, it is quick, so I'll have another go and see if I can find an appropriate adviser.

records.title: IVA - Is it a good idea ?
records.text: I found McCambridge Duffy to be efficient, helpful and non-judgemental. Things were quite straight forward all in all, and they were happy to answer any questions I had along the way.  Of course as with any company dealing in IVA's MCCambride Duffy will receive good money for their work, but the good news is for those applying for the IVA that this is not out of their pocket, but the creditors. AN amount is agreed upon between the creditors and McCambridge Duffy but your payments are not affected. I felt it was my best option, as with the amount I owed,and what I was paying each month was no longer viable. My payments have been cut in half now each month, and although an IVA lasts five years (unless I can pay more into it quicker) the end result is less money paid out by myself than if I had kept going the way I was with high interest loans. It is worth looking into for peace of mind and to stop juggling so many creditors (I had about 10 and was going a little crazy from the constant calls when I missed payments I could no longer afford) Glad I have done it now.

records.title: I started my IVA with them and had …
records.text: I started my IVA with them and had £12,200 debt. After 3 years I had £2700 left to pay due to being made redundant and they took all money from me. I received £5000 PPI all of which was taken from me and money was paid off. I was told that the remaining £2300 would pay off the charges to this company and creditors. My IVA is now over and will be 6 years in December, I received a letter from the PPI company last week that they calculated it wrong and I was due £450. Guess what McCambridge Duffy have taken the money again for all my IVA is over and said its to pay charges to creditors.So really instead of all the nonsense that says get at IVA they will write off up to 75 % of your debt...don't believe it you end up paying back it all back and in my case £2k more.

records.title: Today was the straw that broke the camels back for me - Ref CR0209
records.text: Initially my first impressions of McCambridge Duffy were very good from the introducer Colin Reynolds, to the staff who helped set up my IVA which came about at a low point in my life of being diagnosed with PTSD after a bad assault at work.  This seemed to change after my IVA was set up in February 2011, with mistakes made on several occasions with income and expenditure sheets reverting to the previous years figures and an accusation that I had not paid overtime funds which were due, even though they had been paid months before. This was eventually resolved and I thought at the time that some members of staff there were very rude in their speech and telephone manner. I managed to complete my IVA early in June 2013, one of the reasons being that I no longer wished to have any further dealings, but imagine my astonishment today when i found that they still have a restriction in place on my residential property, even though this should have been removed at the time of the closure. Furthermore i felt that the member of staff i dealt with today was very rude on the phone and I have not been assured that this matter will be dealt with expeditiously in fact it is stopping me remortgaging. Personally I regret ever choosing this company as my IVA supervisor 30/03/2016 - I have today received an email from McCambridge Duffy that the restriction on my property will be removed and that the RX4 will be sent today. This is still completely unacceptable though in that it has delayed a remortgage and caused me additional stress etc when I'm still having ongoing check ups after having hodgkin lymphoma cancer

records.title: Light years ahead of Nationwide
records.text: Compared to my old Nationwide app, this First Direct app is light years ahead. Firstly the ability to pay in cheques via the app instead of having to either send them off in an envelope or do a special journey to a branch. Secondly the payment alerts whenever money comes in or goes out is superb, both for keeping track of finances and for security. The only problem I had was that I had to re-enter details of some companies whose details had been passed over from my previous account as First Direct group them into separate categories depending on whether they're personal accounts or business ones. Other than that I've been very pleased with the operation of the app and very glad I moved from Nationwide.

I use other banks and stockbrokers for non-routine services, but for routine banking I can happily recommend Firstdirect.

records.title: I’ve been with FD for a very long time…
records.text: I’ve been with first direct for a very long time, I’d say it was over 20 years but it might be a bit less. I moved from HSBC and Nat West before that. I loved being able to do stuff over the phone rather than going into branch in the early years and have used the app for online banking for quite a long time. I used to like getting the weekly mini statements as text messages but that’s gone now, and I can review it on the bank feed. I used to find it difficult to get statements as I expect these to be in the bottom options not the 3 dots and used to regularly ask the FAQs how to do this but the convenience to produce a statement when needed and not have to hunt around the house for them is a bonus. I also love the fingerprint login as generating the secure key PIN was also a bit fiddly. I do very occasionally speak to the bank if I have a query or unrecognised transaction and they’ve always been great. The banking just gets easier to do and is all on one place.

records.text: I've been banking with First Direct for more years than I can remember. I've never been dissatisfied with their customer service or, indeed, their service overall. The app makes it very easy to keep an eye on my expenditure and if I have any problems a phone call solves it. On-line or over the phone I feel fully supported. The only thing missing, which I would find useful, is the ability to move money into 'pots' within the account to help budget for future expenses.

records.title: Their Switch Guarantee is WORTHLESS!
records.text: We switched to first direct in September 2022 and since that time, have found most of their customer service excellent. The fly in the ointment, however, was a failure by our old bank to switch all of our direct debits over to first direct, causing a humiliating experience in the spring of 2023, when a requested council bill was not paid.Oddly, the Financial Ombudsman Service clarified today, that neither the old bank (which did not submit the direct debit in question to first direct), NOR first direct (which offered a Switch Guarantee), were at fault!A warning that people should take such guarantees with a LARGE PINCH OF SALT.Edit: Can't exactly say I'm loving it, when you can honour your promises.

records.title: App spot on…
records.text: I use the app regularly to check activity, balance etc. Easy to use, quick and accurate  Spot on, in essence.

records.title: Still good but slipping!
records.text: I have been a customer for many years and have stayed with First Direct, despite the miserable rates of interest they pay, because of their great customer service. However, continued problems with one time passcodes not arriving mean I rarely use my First Direct Credit cared any more. Also, the Move Money section on the website quickly gets clogged up with repeat payments - which are tedious to remove.

records.title: Middle of the road
records.text: Very new customer. I have opened three accounts with them: current account, linked savings and a credit card. I also have accounts with Nationwide, Starling and Chase. I’m in the process of moving my Starling account to FD.My first impression is that the functionality within the mobile app feels a little archaic and the ‘What’s New’ section of the app suggests to me the team at FD are pretty far behind (relative to other banking providers) when it comes to self-serve functionality. I’m hoping to see some improvements in that space. For example it doesn’t look like I can make additional payments to my FD credit card from the app (maybe I can if I set it up as a distinct payee) nor can I self serve ad-hoc payments into my ‘linked savings’ account. If I’ve got any of this wrong and the functionality does exist then it’s a discoverability issue.

So ended up at building society !!!! in desperation but they could open an account straight away ! So sad

Hence the 3 stars, no better no worse than the other banking apps I've used so far.

records.title: Complicated process to set up Direct Debit to pay credit card
records.text: Trying to set up a Direct Debit to pay my credit card (from a non-First Direct current account) was a nightmare. To do this online or via the app, you have to use the 'chat' function, which can take ages. You can do this for other banks by filling in a simple form. The agent who originally dealt with my request set up the Direct Debit from my First Direct current account, which was not what I wanted, and the responses were very slow. Gave up and decided to telephone, and my query was dealt with fairly quickly. I am accustomed to doing things like this myself online, and am very surprised that First Direct does not provide this facility. The app is not particularly intuitive in comparison with those from other banks.

Offered FD suggestions many times to improve the app UX but doesn't seem like something they are interested in improving.

records.title: Excellent service, very competitive exchange rates
records.text: WISE offers an excellent service and very competitive exchange rates (usually, much better than most banks). The card makes your life easier when travelling abroad. records.text: Used Wise for a trip around Europe and UK, stopover in Singapore also. Easy to transfer money to/from, and accepted everywhere we travelled. Use it at home now, although infrequently. Will keep it as we intend travelling again soon. Low fees, nothing negative to say.

records.title: Worldwide coverage
records.text: Over the past 2 years, I have travelled to Australia, Canada, Fiji,  Singapore, Spain, Switzerland and USA. In each Country I have used my Wise card with no issues other than petrol stations in USA  where pay at pump is frequently declined. Having Jars,  the interest gained more than offsets ATM fees and access to cash withdrawals is easy.I have also  saved a substantial amount of money in currency exchanges. A highly recommended product. Many thanks to the unknown person who first introduced me to Wise.

records.text: We are enormously happy with Wise. We love that a digital and physical card can be used. It has been fabulous! However, I respectfully request Wise consider two things: 1) Allow a partner/spouse to be included on a joint account and 2) allow a partner/spouse to be designated as a beneficiary when one passes away.

records.title: Best rates, instant and trustworthy.
records.text: Best rates, instant and trustworthy. I don't normally respond to requests for reviews, but Wise  deserve it. Deposits, currency purchases and payments within and outside of UK made in seconds. I recommend everyone gets a Wise account.

records.title: Ideal solution for travel money
records.text: Wise has been my preferred option for my international currency needs - be it travelling or paying for services in various currencies around the world, knowing I'm getting a fair exchange rate. What I really love is the automatic use of funds from one currency, when the currency I need has run out.And my #1 experience was in Mexico, where I urgently needed to transfer some money to/from my normal bank account but my bank locked me out (as I tried logging in from abroad). Wise saved me as I could still move money there. I still needed to log in to Wise and they required a verification code for my login but they offered to send it via Whatsapp instead of a celular network (which I couldn't access from there as my roaming wasn't working). I'm an even bigger fan of Wise since then.

There is no live chat and a lot of loops (as in they keep redirecting you back to the same FAQ pages) when trying to reach out for support on a transaction.Their great rates on exchange are most valuable when exchanging larger sums but unfortunately their lack of transparency creates a lot of stress when you see large amounts of money leave your bank account and seemingly disappear because it's not showing "within minutes" as advertised. So I've increased my rating from 1 star to 2 stars because they did fix the problem after nearly 4 months of sending information to their support.

records.title: Do NOT use this firm for debt advice or…
records.text: Do NOT use this firm for debt advice or management !I managed to get myself into a position where i was struggling with debt. Stepchange was suggested, went online & then spoke with Stepchange, or who i thought was stepchange, I was told about Clear start through them, so after the call ended was almost immediately called by Osman at Clear start... Now this is where you get sucked in, they are very helpful here, baffle you with information & promises of how your debt can be reduced or at least payments lowered...by the end your head is spinning a bit & they are very good at making you feel like you'll get somewhere... Well, 4 months later, all i am is £700+ lighter in their fees & knee deep in creditors  letters as i was told to stop paying & pretty much ignore letters & calls ! They call every so often, baffle you with bull again & make sure they still have your card details to take your money ! I am usually pretty shrewd & savvy, but going through stepchange & paying a company I assumed (very wrongly) that things would get sorted fast... Please dont fall for this shoddy company, there are many reviews out there now saying the same as me, unfortunately i saw a few reviews from people & thought they maybe weren't doing something correctly, that is not the case. please don't use any company that asks for a payment, use the free ones.

records.title: Update to my previous (Google) review of Clear…
records.text: Update to my previous review of Clear Start Accountants. (Please go to Google review to see my initial review).I felt compelled to update my review following Clear Start Accountants' response to my initial feedback. Their reaction has only reinforced my disappointment with their service.After posting my first review, they quickly responded (same day), claiming to be "disappointed" with my feedback. They asserted they had been in "constant communication" with my new accountant and that there were still seven items needing review. They requested I consider removing my review based on this.However, their claims couldn't be further from the truth. Today is 8th November, I wrote my original review on the 8th October, since that time:	1. My new accountant is still chasing them for things he needs to be able to close move on with my accounts. 	2. I haven't had an update regarding the seven items that were mentioned only assume they are still unresolved, I can only assume they are still unresolved over a month later.	3. In my email to them on the 9th I asked them to respond to three specific request, they didn't even acknowledge the email. This radio silence further demonstrates their lack of professionalism and disregard for client concerns. It's clear that their swift response to my review was merely an attempt to save face rather than a genuine effort to address the issues.Their behaviour throughout this process - from the initial delays to their recent lack of follow-through - demonstrates a consistent pattern of poor service and communication.If you're seeking an accountancy firm that values your time, maintains open communication, and delivers on their promises, I strongly advise looking elsewhere. My experience suggests that Clear Start Accountants falls significantly short in these crucial areas.Clear Start Accountants have had ample opportunity to rectify the situation but have consistently failed to do so. Potential clients should consider themselves warned.
